measures.questionText: Shall the Township Committee of the Township of West Amwell amend Chapter 35, Section 35-3 of the Township Code, entitled “Funding,” to provide that the Municipal Open Space, Farmland and Recreation and Historic Preservation Trust Fund shall be funded by an annual tax levy in an amount up to, but not exceeding, $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation, rather than requiring the annual levy to be set at $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation?
measures.officialStatement: A “Yes” vote authorizes the Township Committee to amend Section 35-3 of the Township Code so that the annual dedicated levy for the Municipal Open Space, Farmland and Recreation and Historic Preservation Trust Fund may be set each year in an amount up to, but not exceeding, $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation. The current ordinance provides for an annual levy of exactly $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation. Approval of this question would not increase the maximum authorized open space levy. Instead, it would allow the Township Committee to levy less than $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation in a particular year if the Township Committee determines that a lower levy is appropriate. Funds raised by the levy would continue to be dedicated to the purposes authorized for the Municipal Open Space, Farmland and Recreation and Historic Preservation Trust Fund, including open space, recreation, farmland preservation, historic preservation, and related purposes authorized by law. A “No” vote means Section 35-3 would remain unchanged, and the ordinance would continue to provide for an annual levy of $0.06 per $100.00 of assessed valuation.

measures.questionText: Shall the Board of Education of the Bloomsbury School District be permitted to join the North Hunterdon-Voorhees Regional High School District as a constituent member with the tax apportionment formula to remain 100% on each municipality’s equalized valuation allocated to the regional district as provided by state law and with the membership of the North Hunterdon- Vorhees Regional Board of Education to be expanded to 13 members with such membership to be apportioned utilizing the same methodology currently utilized by the North Hunterdon-Voorhees Regional Board of Education.
measures.officialStatement: Beginning with the 2025-26 school year, students from Bloomsbury began attending North Hunterdon High School through a sending-receiving (contractual) relationship. Regardless of whether this referendum passes, Bloomsbury students will continue to attend North Hunterdon High School. If this referendum passes, Bloomsbury will become a constituent member of the North Hunterdon-Voorhees Regional High School District. As a constituent member, Bloomsbury residents will gain voting representation on the Regional Board of Education, and Bloomsbury’s share of the regional district’s costs will be allocated based on equalized property valuation, consistent with the Regional District’s current and long-standing practice and state law. The Regional Board of Education will expand from 12 to 13 members, with seats apportioned based on census population data and updated following each decennial census. Based on the 2020 Census, the initial seat allocation would be as follows: • Bethlehem Township and Hampton Borough: 1 representative (elected at-large) • Union Township and Bloomsbury: 2 representatives (elected at-large) • Califon Borough and Tewksbury Township: 2 representatives (elected at-large) • Clinton Township and Lebanon Borough: 4 representatives (elected at-large) • High Bridge Borough and Lebanon Township: 2 representatives (elected at-large) • Town of Clinton, Franklin Township, and Glen Gardner Borough: 2 representatives (elected at-large) If this referendum does not pass, Bloomsbury students will continue to attend North Hunterdon High School under the existing sending-receiving relationship. However, Bloomsbury would not become a constituent member of the regional district, would not have voting representation on the Regional Board of Education, unless and until it sends a sufficient percentage of students to meet the statutory threshold, and would continue to pay tuition under the terms of the sending- receiving agreement rather than contributing through the regional tax apportionment formula.

The current ordinance requires exactly 6 cents per $100 each year. The authorized maximum and the fund’s open-space, recreation, farmland and historic-preservation purposes would stay unchanged.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize changing the ordinance so the Township Committee can choose a lower rate while keeping a 6-cent ceiling.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the requirement to levy exactly 6 cents per $100 of assessed value each year.

measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve replacing the fire-alarm equipment and up to $926,000 in bonds.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Makes Bloomsbury a full constituent member of the North Hunterdon–Voorhees regional high-school district, with its share of district costs based entirely on equalized property value under the existing regional tax formula, rather than tuition under a sending–receiving contract. Bloomsbury students would continue attending North Hunterdon High School whether this proposal passes or fails. The regional board would expand from 12 to 13 members, with seats apportioned by census population and updated after each ten-year census. The initial shared, at-large seat allocation would be: Bethlehem Township and Hampton, one; Union Township and Bloomsbury, two; Califon and Tewksbury, two; Clinton Township and Lebanon Borough, four; High Bridge and Lebanon Township, two; and Clinton Town, Franklin Township and Glen Gardner, two. Approval requires both a majority across the existing 12 regional municipalities combined and a separate majority in Bloomsbury.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve Bloomsbury joining as a constituent member with the proposed tax formula and board representation. Both electorates must approve for the membership change to proceed.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed membership change; Bloomsbury would continue its tuition-based arrangement, with no regional-board voting representation unless it later meets the statutory student-enrollment threshold.

Approval requires both a majority across the existing 12 regional municipalities combined and a separate majority in Bloomsbury.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve Bloomsbury joining as a constituent member with the proposed tax formula and board representation. Both electorates must approve for the membership change to proceed.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed membership change; Bloomsbury would continue its tuition-based arrangement, with no regional-board voting representation unless it later meets the statutory student-enrollment threshold.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes the Holland school board to spend $11,550,060 and issue up to that amount in bonds for improvements at Holland Township School. The work includes roof replacement, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning improvements, replacement of asbestos flooring, fixtures, equipment and site work. All $11,550,060 is approved as eligible costs, with the stated state-aid calculation equal to 40% of annual debt payments associated with those costs. The board could transfer funds among projects approved at this election. Question 1 can take effect if approved even when Question 2 is rejected; approving both would authorize $15,972,660 in total project costs and bonds.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these projects and up to $11,550,060 in bonds, independently of whether Question 2 passes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project and bond authorization; Question 2 also could not take effect without Question 1’s approval.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes the Holland school board to spend $4,422,600 and issue up to that amount in bonds for additional improvements at Holland Township School, only if Question 1 also passes at this election. The work includes replacing windows; renovating bathrooms, lockers, flooring, classrooms and the multipurpose room; installing an alarm; and related fixtures, furniture, equipment and site work. All $4,422,600 is approved as eligible costs, with the stated state-aid calculation equal to 40% of annual debt payments associated with those costs. The board could transfer funds among approved projects; approving both questions would authorize $15,972,660 in total project costs and bonds.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these additional projects and up to $4,422,600 in bonds, taking effect only if Question 1 is also approved.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this additional project and bond authorization; Question 1 could still take effect if separately approved.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes the Flemington–Raritan regional school board to spend $30,320,944 and issue up to that amount in bonds for improvements, alterations, renovations and upgrades, with equipment, fixtures, site work and related costs. Projects cover J.P. Case Middle School, Reading-Fleming Intermediate School, Barley Sheaf Elementary, Copper Hill Elementary, Francis A. Desmares Elementary and Robert Hunter Elementary. All $30,320,944 is approved as eligible costs: $9,732,750 at J.P. Case, $8,874,000 at Reading-Fleming, $2,825,000 at Barley Sheaf, $1,303,250 at Copper Hill, $1,145,750 at Desmares and $6,440,194 at Robert Hunter. The stated state-aid calculation is 40% of annual debt payments associated with those eligible costs; the board could transfer money among projects approved at this election.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these school improvements and up to $30,320,944 in bonds.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes Lambertville Fire District No. 1 to spend up to $7.5 million on three fire trucks, related equipment and improvements at the firehouse at 230 North Main Street. The trucks are a fire engine, an engine tanker and an engine ladder truck. Firehouse work includes an addition and renovation, work on existing truck bays, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning, paving, curbs, sidewalks and related site work. The district could finance the projects with bonds, short-term bond-anticipation notes, lease-purchase financing, or a combination of those options.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve spending up to $7.5 million for the listed equipment and firehouse projects and the proposed financing options.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this capital-project spending and financing authorization.
